children: Our Bureau Mumbai: New India Assurance Company (NIACL) reported a net loss of 1,267 crore in the September quarter, against a net profit of 63 crore in the corresponding period last year, as underwriting losses widened amid adverse claims experience in property, motor and health insurance.

Gross written premium (GWP) rose 5.2% year on year to 11,083 crore from 10,541 crore, the state-owned general insurer said in its earnings release. "This second quarter has been one of the most challenging quarters for the company in recent times, more so while succeeding another equally challenging one for the entire industry," said Lavanya R Mundayur, chairman and MD. "This quarter, GWP grew by only 5.1%, primarily due to the steep decline in property rates. " Net premium written increased marginally by 0.5% to 8,850 crore, while net premium earned grew 2.5% to 9,632 crore. Underwriting loss widened to 5,237 crore in the quarter from 3,554 crore a year earlier.

title: New India Slips into Red on Underwriting Losses
